subject: Service degradation impacting HarborFin — remediation & contract reconvene
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@harborfin.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: Megan Li <megan@harborfin.com>, ops@harborfin.com
Date: 2026-05-20T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: Production degradation — 05/20 (latency + 500s) impacting end-of-day settlements

Jonas,

We hit a severe degradation window this morning and again at 17:40 PT when request latencies spiked above 1.2s and error rates climbed to ~14% for the /v1/generate endpoint. This impacted our end-of-day settlement jobs and caused a cascade of pipeline retries. Ops attached a quick timeline.

We need two things immediately:
- a remediation timeline and concrete mitigation steps for tonight's batch job (we're planning another run at 20:00 PT)
- confirmation of Redwood's position on SLA credits for the affected windows — this incident materially impacted revenue recognition for us.

Please escalate to your leadership; Megan and I will be on standby.

Attachments: [Attachment: incident-timeline.csv (CSV, 9KB)]

Sanjay Rao
Head of Platform Engineering, HarborFin
sanjay@harborfin.com
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@harborfin.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-20T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production degradation — 05/20 (latency + 500s) impacting end-of-day settlements

Sanjay —

Thanks for the heads up and for sending the timeline. I'm very sorry for the disruption; we take incidents like this seriously. Quick updates and immediate actions: 

- We've routed your production traffic to an alternate pool (same model) to reduce queuing. This should cut the observed p95 in half within 10–15 minutes.
- Marcus is running a short KV-cache warmup and rekey to clear any fragmented cache entries that may have amplified latency for long sequences.
- Laura and I are pulling the full traces and will share a draft incident summary within 90 minutes.

On credits: we will need to review the incident window and internal telemetry to calculate an SLA credit. I will coordinate with Hannah (our Head of Customer Success) to expedite a remediation offer and a transparent credit calculation. Can you confirm whether HarborFin considers the 17:40–18:05 PT window the primary impact period for accounting?

I'll keep this line live; if helpful we can jump on a 15-minute call now.

— Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai
From: Megan Li <megan@harborfin.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-20T09:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production degradation — 05/20 (latency + 500s) impacting end-of-day settlements

Jonas — thanks for the quick routing. To confirm: HarborFin's finance team is flagging the 17:40–18:10 PT window as the exposure for today's settlements. We will share a short damage estimate (lost trade count) within the hour.

As context, this is the second notable degradation in the past quarter; we need a remediation plan that includes both near-term operational mitigations and a contractual fix (credits + a remediation runbook).

Megan
Platform Ops, HarborFin
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-21T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Production degradation — request for SLA credit and remediation runbook

Hannah — forwarding the HarborFin thread. Key facts:
- Impact window identified as 2026-05-20 17:40–18:10 PT (customer claim).
- Symptoms: sustained p95 latency >1s, error rate ~14%, throughput drops on heavy batch loads.
- HarborFin requests: immediate remediation for tonight's 20:00 job, SLA credit calculation, and a remediation runbook/contractual fix (quarterly credits or a guaranteed burst pool).

Proposed internal ask:
1) Offer an immediate operational remediation we can guarantee tonight (we already routed traffic; need to confirm p95 improvements).
2) Propose a one-time credit equivalent to 25% of the billed tokens for the impacted hourly windows while we complete root cause analysis. This is a placeholder — finance/legal will need to sign off.
3) Draft a remediation runbook (attached) and propose a contract amendment that: commits a reserved burst pool for peak batch windows, provides automatic failover to a second region, and defines a credit schedule if similar degradation reoccurs within 90 days.

Attachments: [Attachment: proposed-remedy-draft.pdf (PDF, 42KB)]

Questions: do we want to include a goodwill executive call (Jonas + CEO) if HarborFin elevates this to their CFO? Laura, Marcus — can you validate the 25% placeholder and propose a cleaner calculation?

— Jonas

On Fri, 2026-05-20 at 09:02 Jonas wrote:
> Sanjay —
> 
> Thanks for the heads up and for sending the timeline. I'm very sorry for the disruption; we take incidents like this seriously. Quick updates and immediate actions: 
> 
> - We've routed your production traffic to an alternate pool (same model) to reduce queuing. This should cut the observed p95 in half within 10–15 minutes.

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@harborfin.com>, Megan Li <megan@harborfin.com>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-22T16:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production degradation — 05/20 (latency + 500s) impacting end-of-day settlements

Sanjay / Megan —

Thanks for your patience while we pulled the telemetry and structured a remediation offer. Below is our proposed path forward; happy to jump on an executive call this week to finalize.

Summary of action and offer:
1) Immediate operational remediation (completed 2026-05-20): traffic reroute + cache rekey reduced p95 by ~48% within 20 minutes; we added a policy to keep a warm burst pool during your nightly batches.

2) Credit proposal (draft): Redwood proposes a one-time credit equal to 20% of HarborFin's billed tokens for the affected billing hour (17:00–18:00 PT on 2026-05-20). We arrived at 20% after weighing the severity, repeat incidents, and our standard SLA matrix. This is subject to finance approval; we can convert to a prorated dollar credit in an amendment.

3) Contract remediation / runbook: attached is a draft amendment that adds:
   - Guaranteed burst pool (reserved capacity during scheduled nightly batches)
   - Automatic region failover for production-critical routes during scheduled batch windows
   - Quarterly joint incident review and a 90-day conditional credit schedule if similar degradations reoccur

Attachments: [Attachment: incident-timeline.csv (CSV, 9KB)], [Attachment: proposed-remedy-draft.pdf (PDF, 42KB)]

Next steps we propose:
- HarborFin confirms acceptance of the 20% credit or counters with a figure by 2026-05-24 EOD PT.
- Sign the amendment (DocuSign link below) to lock in the burst pool and failover commitments.
- Schedule an exec call if HarborFin's CFO wants a direct conversation (Jonas + Laura + Hannah + HarborFin CFO).

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/link/HF-REM-20260522
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/67890

We appreciate the candid feedback and want to make this right for HarborFin.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Enterprise Account Lead, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai
